name: Round games/card (poker) table — green baize inset in a turned wood rim, frieze drawer, cabriole legs
description: A small round antique English games table for the 3D poker scene: a solid-wood top with a raised turned lip, a cross-band inlay line, and a green woollen-BAIZE playing inset sitting proud in the well; a frieze apron with a single drawer + drop brass pull; 4 simplified slender legs (cabriole in the reference). Shape is plain, the VISIBLE TOP is the detailed part. Materials: oak/walnut wood + brass + the new 'baize' green cloth.

parts.name: Solid-wood round top slab (the wood you see around the cloth)
parts.note: Top slab; top surface at y=0.730 (height 730 mm), 34 mm thick. Ø1380 = antique Ø920 enlarged ~50% for the 6-max poker scene (owner-directed upsize, dossier#overall + needs[]).

parts.name: Green woollen-baize playing surface (fills the top to the edge)
parts.note: Owner: bigger playing surface, NO raised lip — the green reaches right to the edge. Baize Ø≈1344 fills almost the whole Ø1380 top, leaving only a thin ~18 mm wood edge; rests on the slab top (bottom 0.730), ~13 mm proud. kind:'baize' on texturedCylinder maps a high-res woven-cloth CanvasTexture (warp/weft weave + brushed-nap mottle + lamp-pool vignette + faint dealer rings) onto the top cap, so the felt reads as real napped wool up close instead of a flat green disc; seg 80 keeps the rim round.

parts.name: Frieze apron band under the top (holds the drawer)
parts.note: 100 mm frieze, set in from the 0.69 top edge so the top overhangs ~90 mm; spans y 0.596–0.696 (meets slab bottom).

parts.name: Single frieze drawer front
parts.note: Shallow drawer front proud of the apron front; darker wood reads the drawer box.

parts.name: Drop-pull brass backplate
parts.note: Small brass backplate for the teardrop pull, proud of the drawer front.

parts.name: Drop/teardrop brass pull
parts.note: Teardrop drop pull (rendered as a small brass boss) hanging just below the backplate centre.

parts.name: Four slender legs (cabriole in the reference; simplified to plain posts)
parts.note: 4 legs spread under the enlarged Ø1380 top — span 0.78 m (corner reach ~0.55 < 0.60 apron radius < 0.69 top radius) so they stay TUCKED under the overhang yet support the big top sensibly. 60 mm posts into the apron; cabriole curve omitted per owner brief.

needs: Top enlarged to Ø1380 mm — an owner-directed ~50% upsize for the 6-max poker scene that EXCEEDS the antique sourced range (Ø700–950); height kept at 730 mm (dossier#overall). A gameplay decision, not a measurement.
Top slab thickness / rim-band width / raised-lip / reveal are PHOTO-DERIVED (dossier#top_construction)
Cabriole leg curve + pad feet are NOT modelled — plain slender posts stand in per owner brief; knee/foot dims derived
Drawer is a front + pull only (no opening box); frieze depth derived
Baize colour is the conventional billiard green (palette 'baize'), no standard hex
Cross-band inlay is suggested by a thin darker torus line, not a true veneer band
